A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tropical Attention work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on eleven combinatorial tasks, including OOD performance in Tables 1–2 and attention-map analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports revised combinatorial experiments, Universal Transformer comparisons, inference measurements, and Tropical Transformer results on Long Range Arena.

M1.justification: Equation 2 replaces subtraction of a learnable shift with explicit row-maximum subtraction in the tropicalization map. The remaining MHTA operations are retained. Algorithm 1 still specifies the learned shift, leaving the implemented normalization ambiguous despite the changed formula.

E1.justification: v2 adds five Long Range Arena tasks spanning mathematical, text, retrieval, and image inputs. Appendix E also revises retained task requirements: several scalar optimization targets become token-wise solution masks, Fractional Knapsack predicts per-item fractions, and SCC changes from symmetrized connectivity to directed strongly connected components with communities.

E2.justification: Length-OOD comparisons add vanilla and adaptive-softmax Universal Transformers with dynamic halting. The new LRA comparison also includes Longformer, Linformer, Performer, Elliptical Attention, Fourierformer, and MEGA, mostly through source-reported baseline scores. These methods were not evaluated comparators in v1.

E3.justification: The reported training sample count increases from 100k to 10M, while Balanced Partition and Bin Packing change from 1000 to 100 epochs. Four former regression tasks are evaluated using classification Micro-F1. v2 also introduces 32-step recurrent baselines, LRA accuracy evaluation, and CPU/GPU timing comparisons; these are substantial reported setting changes.

E4.justification: New Table 2 examines computational efficiency through inference time and parameter counts. The existing random-perturbation robustness procedure and Quickselect/Knapsack attention-map analyses remain; renaming adversarial testing as perturbative noise does not establish a new attack analysis, and the heatmap image content is reused.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates only, whereas v2 Tables 1 and 3 introduce ± terms throughout the main three-model combinatorial comparisons. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting, but their meaning, run counts, and seeds are unspecified; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: The combinatorial results are extensively replaced. For example, Quickselect Value-OOD Micro-F1 changes from 0/0/44 to 74.22/74.30/71.10 for Vanilla/Adaptive/Tropical, reversing the reported ranking under revised training conditions. New recurrent-baseline, LRA, timing, and parameter-count results further expand the evidence; these are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The original circuit-universality and DP-simulation results largely survive as Appendix C. v2 adds a finite Kleene-star definition, Theorem C.5 and its proof claiming transitive-closure realization, and Corollary C.5.1 concerning shortest paths. Remark 3.1 additionally distinguishes potentially exponential shallow width from polynomial-resource depth.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add central claims about transitive closure without explicit recurrence and inference/parameter advantages over recurrent models. v2 newly claims the first extension of neural algorithmic reasoning to NP-hard/complete problems, although those problem families already appeared in v1. Adversarial-robustness claims are reframed around perturbative noise.

C2.justification: v2 develops the interpretation that MHTA learns closure directly instead of recurrently refining states, while acknowledging potentially exponential width for shallow realizations. LRA results support a new general-purpose sequence-modeling interpretation. The limitations narrow from untested language/vision applications to generative, autoregressive language tasks, retaining the computational-overhead caveat.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit repository and data-loader links and refines dataset-generation documentation with positional features, repeated capacities, solver choices, and canonical DP tracebacks. Much of the existing backbone, optimizer, hardware, and batch-size documentation remains. These disclosures do not establish that the linked resources were newly released.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around recurrent Transformers, neuroalgebraic geometry, semiring algorithms, and efficient long-sequence attention. It adds relevant citations and explicitly distinguishes its geometric approach from earlier tropical-arithmetic approaches, alongside the new novelty claim concerning NP-hard/complete problems.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten, with substantial revisions to methodological explanations and discussion. Tropical-geometry background moves from Section 2.3 to Appendix B, limitations move to Appendix A, and dataset descriptions are reorganized and rewritten beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: The original regression/classification tables are reorganized into separate length-OOD and value/noise displays, with recurrent-baseline columns and uncertainty annotations. New efficiency and LRA tables are added. Existing heatmaps are retained but redistributed and resized, with expanded captions and a prominent early length-OOD table.

improvement.justification: Broader LRA coverage, stronger comparators, efficiency measurements, and clearer noise terminology provide meaningful benefits. However, the newly central Theorem C.5 equates repeated multiplication by D with a truncated Kleene-star sum, which its stated recurrence does not compute. Equation 2 also conflicts with the retained pseudocode. Table 4 reports a Tropical average of 72.79 although its five scores average 72.19, without changing second place. These substantive inconsistencies alongside the empirical gains prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
